title: BOX OF 1980'S BIRD FIGURINES, ...
description: BOX OF 1980'S BIRD FIGURINES, SHELLEY VASE ETC
findings: All 3 photos checked, with enlarged crops of the base. The vase is genuine Shelley by its marks: green printed shield cartouche 'MADE IN SHELLEY ENGLAND', black printed 'Rd 680712', and hand-written black numbers read as 8433 and 108 (orientation uncertain). Rd 680712 falls in 1921 on Carlton Ware World's registered design table (680147 to 687143 = 1921; https://carltonwareworld.com/registered-design-numbers.htm, read 19 Oct 2026), so the design dates from 1921 and this piece is probably 1920s. Decoration is hand-painted: black shoulder band with purple and green butterflies and a white dotted border above a bright yellow body on a short foot, mid-sized (exact height not stated). This is the Shelley Art Deco butterfly vase type; the pattern number 8433 itself was not confirmed online, but Carters (Australian auctioneer) lists 'Two Art Deco Shelley butterfly vases' (carters.com.au item 1388417, title seen in search results 19 Oct 2026, page not opened so no price seen), so the type is traded. Other items in the box: two tall pink swan or flamingo figurines with gilt beaks (1980s style), a small pale blue Wedgwood style jasper dish, a fluted bowl with posy decoration and gilt foot, and two cream jugs with pink rose sprays; none show a legible mark (bases not photographed).
condition: Vase shows no chips, cracks or crazing in the photos, only a tiny speck in the yellow glaze and light staining and wear on the base rim. Jugs, bowl and figurines look intact from the front; bases not shown.
reason: Genuine hand-painted Shelley Art Deco butterfly vase with shield mark and Rd number (1921 design), plus other china.
marks_read: MADE IN SHELLEY ENGLAND (green shield); Rd 680712; hand-written 8433 and 108

Unboxed: a green 0-6-0 tank loco with brass dome, a black BR 2-6-4T loco numbered 80059 or 80069, a GWR green 4-4-0 loco and tender with maroon chassis (number not legible), a loose steam loco chassis, a red and yellow crane wagon, four GWR chocolate and cream clerestory coaches, two green coach shells, a Tri-ang yellow-box turntable set with extra points and a controller, a Hornby Dublo instruction booklet, Tri-ang catalogue and leaflets, a tunnel kit in a blue box (maker not legible), grey plastic girder bridge and station kit parts, a Faller glue bottle and a large tray of track and points. reason: Large lot of mostly boxed 1960s to 70s Tri-ang Hornby locos, coaches and wagons plus a turntable under a generic title; value is in the sum of many collectable pieces.
marks_read: Tri-ang Hornby Model Railways box printing; BR Freightliner logos; Lima OH box (Esso tanker); Hornby Dublo instruction booklet; Faller bottle; loco number 80059 or 80069; box label code partly legible (R.33?)

title: ROYAL DOULTON COFFEE POT, LAWN...
description: ROYAL DOULTON COFFEE POT, LAWN BOWLS, FLASK ETC
findings: All 4 photos checked, with enlarged crops of the pot, clock and flask. Royal Doulton seriesware coffee pot carrying the printed pattern title 'GAFFERS' on the body and on the lid: an old man in a smock and top hat with a basket and stick beside a cottage with hollyhocks, black handle and ring finial. The Doulton Collectors Club says the Gaffers pattern was introduced in 1921 and designed by C J Noke (https://doultoncollectorsclub.com/2014/07/11/royal-doultons-gaffers-seriesware/, read 19 Oct 2026). The Royal Doulton backstamp itself is not visible in the photos (catalogue title says Royal Doulton). Other items: a glazed ceramic figure group of a courting couple in 18th century dress on a black painted base (unmarked); a ceramic mantel clock with two birds of paradise in pink, lilac and yellow lustre glaze with gilt, gilt bezel and a plain white dial with no legible brand (a small black script mark on the front is unreadable); a cream pilgrim-style flask with a coloured relief figure of a lawn bowler and a green glazed back and foot (maker not visible); and a brown mottled cane handle with brass collar.
condition: Coffee pot has a dark seam line at the spout and body junction that suggests a crack or old repair (needs inspection); lid appears to fit. Figure group has flaking paint, losses and a base cracked in several places and glued. Clock working order unknown. Flask shows no chips from the front; base not shown.
reason: Royal Doulton Gaffers seriesware coffee pot is the best item, though the spout joint may be damaged; the rest is low value.
